# `mem` standard library

The `mem` module provides unified, explicit memory management:
low-level byte operations, regional bump arenas, and fixed-capacity object pools.
The [arena runtime contract](https://gitea.gde.to/ike/dva/wiki/spec-std-mem.-)
documents scope switching, marks, generation invalidation, and arena lifetimes.

```{.dva .run}
#use mem
```

## Low-level memory utilities

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mem::copy` | `Addr, Addr, Int => ()` | Copies `bytes` count from source to destination |
| `mem::move` | `Addr, Addr, Int => ()` | Copies `bytes` count with support for overlap |
| `mem::zero` | `Addr, Int => ()` | Fills memory range with zeros |
| `mem::set` | `Addr, Int, Int => ()` | Fills memory range with specified byte value |
| `mem::align_forward` | `Addr, Int => Addr` | Advances address to meet alignment requirement |
| `mem::is_aligned` | `Addr, Int => <>` | Checks whether address satisfies alignment |
| `mem::index_byte` | `Addr, Int, Int => < Int | >` | `memchr(3)`: offset of the first `byte` in `[p, p + len)`, or `<-->` if absent |

## Regional bump arenas

Arenas provide allocation without per-object free overhead. All allocations
within an arena are freed simultaneously when the arena is reset or destroyed.

```{.dva .run}
#type Arena (raw: Addr, cap: Int)
#type ArenaStats (bytes_allocated: Int, num_chunks: Int, cap: Int)
#type ArenaProvenance (arena: Addr, generation: Int, scope_depth: Int,
   resets: Int, bytes_allocated: Int, num_chunks: Int)
```

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mem::arena` | `Int => Arena` | Creates an arena with initial chunk capacity (bytes) |
| `mem::arena_default` | `() => Arena` | Creates an arena with default 64 MB chunk capacity |
| `mem::global_arena` | `() => Arena` | Returns the persistent thread-default global arena descriptor |
| `mem::current` | `() => Addr` | Returns the active arena descriptor (global arena when no scoped arena is selected) |
| `mem::set_current` | `Addr => Addr` | Selects an arena and returns the previously active descriptor; `Addr(0)` selects the global arena |
| `mem::save` | `Arena => Int` | Saves an allocation mark in the given arena |
| `mem::restore_to` | `Arena, Int => ()` | Restores the arena to a mark returned by `save` |
| `mem::alloc` | `Arena, Int => Addr` | Allocates uninitialized memory of given byte size |
| `mem::reset` | `Arena => ()` | Rewinds arena offset to zero, retaining chunks |
| `mem::release` | `Arena => ()` | Frees backing chunks while keeping the arena descriptor reusable |
| `mem::destroy` | `Arena => ()` | Frees all backing chunks and arena descriptor |
| `mem::stats` | `Arena => ArenaStats` | Retrieves allocation metrics and chunk counts |
| `mem::provenance` | `Arena => ArenaProvenance` | Retrieves generation epoch, scope depth, reset count, and allocation totals |
| `mem::current_provenance` | `() => ArenaProvenance` | Retrieves provenance for the currently active ambient arena |
| `mem::owns_addr` | `Arena, Addr => <>` | Returns `<+>` when `ptr` falls within the live allocated chunks of `a` |
| `mem::with` | `Arena, (() => ()) => ()` | Runs action with arena set as ambient allocator |
| `mem::with_value` | `#param T: Type, Arena, (() => T) => T` | Runs an action in an arena and returns its value |
| `mem::escape` | `(() => ()) => ()` | Runs action in the global arena, restoring the prior arena afterward |
| `mem::escape_value` | `#param T: Type, (() => T) => T` | Runs an action in the global arena and returns its value |

`current` and `set_current` are low-level controls for integrations. Prefer
`with`, `with_value`, `escape`, and `escape_value` for scoped switching because
they restore the previous arena when the callback returns. Marks belong to the
arena passed to `save` and must be restored to that same arena. `release` drops
the arena's chunks but leaves its descriptor valid for later allocations.

```{.dva .run}
#use mem

ar = mem::arena(1024)
buf = mem::alloc(ar, 256)
// ... use buf ...
mem::destroy(ar)
```

## Arena Lifetime & Escape Contract

Every Edva thread has an implicit persistent global arena (`mem::global_arena!`) and an ambient current arena (`mem::current!`). Implicit allocations (`String` concatenation, records, `Builder`, dynamic arrays, maps, boxed ramifications/enums, and closure environments) allocate in whichever arena is ambient at the allocation site.

- **Scalars and bitfields** (`Int`, `i8`..`u64`, `Float`, `f32`, `Rune`, `<>`, `()`, fixed bitfields): passed and returned by value with no arena backing; safe to return across any `mem::with_value`, `mem::reset`, `mem::destroy`, or block restore boundary.
- **Records, nested containers, and boxed unions**: allocated in the ambient arena at construction or growth time (array `+=` doubling, map rehash). A container created in the global arena that grows while a request arena `a` is ambient acquires backing buffers in `a` unless growth runs inside `mem::escape(...)`.
- **Deep string copies (`++s`)**: always allocate a fresh `{ len, data }` string and byte buffer in the *current* ambient arena (stripping scope generation tags). To promote a `String` built inside a request arena `a` so it survives `mem::reset(a)` or `mem::destroy(a)`, copy it inside `mem::escape` or `mem::escape_value` (e.g. `mem::escape_value((!=> ++s))`).
- **Closures & asynchronous callbacks**:
  - Synchronous callbacks invoked strictly before the request arena resets may run inside `mem::with(req, ...)` and capture request-scoped values freely.
  - Deferred / asynchronous callbacks stored beyond `mem::reset(req)` or `mem::destroy(req)` must allocate both the closure environment and any captured strings/records in the persistent arena (construct or promote the callback and its captured values inside `mem::escape`).
  - Capturing closures passed to `mem::with` / `mem::with_value` allocate their capture environment in the caller's active arena *before* switching arenas, so unbounded request loops should pass non-capturing closures or bracket each iteration with `mem::set_current` (or `mem::save` and `mem::restore_to` on the outer arena).
- **Frame-bound views & block-scoped addresses (unsafe boundaries)**:
  - Typed memory views (`@[ptr RecordType]`) borrow external/frame storage without copying. The compiler statically rejects returning a view directly, wrapped in a composite/variant/map, captured in a closure, written to a global, or stored through a field/index write (`E3150`).
  - Taking `&builder` / `&local` inside an implicit top-level arena-restore block produces a block-scoped `Addr`. The compiler statically rejects returning it or any composite/closure holding it (`E3133`), as well as writing it or any composite/closure containing it to an outer variable, member, or element (`E3134`).
  - Runtime scope tags validate mortal `String` reads (`E4010`) and block-scoped `Addr` dereferences (`E4011`) across implicit save/restore scopes. Explicit `mem::save`, `mem::restore_to`, `mem::reset`, and `mem::destroy` bump the arena reset count and generation epoch (`mem::provenance`), and ownership can be queried in tests or debug builds via `mem::owns_addr`.

```{.dva .run}
#use mem

req = mem::arena(4096)
retained: String{}

mem::with(req, !=>
   tmp = "req_" + "ok"
   safe = mem::escape_value((!=> ++tmp))
   mem::escape((!=> retained += safe))
)

mem::reset(req)
prov = mem::provenance(req)
// prov.resets == 1, prov.bytes_allocated == 0
mem::destroy(req)
```

### Thread & Task Arena Ownership

Concurrent execution with `task::spawn` and `task::join` enforces strict per-thread arena isolation:

- **Thread-default base arenas**: On the main thread, `@global_arena` serves as the persistent fallback base arena. Each `task::spawn` worker receives its own heap-allocated child `Arena`, installed as both its ambient arena (`@dva_arena_tls`) and its thread-local base arena (`@dva_arena_base_tls`).
- **`mem::escape` & `mem::global_arena!` inside tasks**: Calling `mem::global_arena!`, `mem::escape`, `mem::escape_value`, or `mem::set_current(Addr(0))` inside a worker resolves to that worker thread's own base arena (`@dva_arena_base_tls`), never the main thread's `@global_arena`. Scoped `mem::with(req, ...)` paired with `mem::escape(...)` inside parallel workers therefore runs lock-free without data races.
- **Handoff & adoption on `task::join`**: `task::spawn` deep-copies arguments and captured closure environments into the worker's child arena before launching the thread. `task::join` waits on the worker (`pthread_join`), deep-copies the returned value (or `Error`) into the joining thread's ambient arena, adopts any surviving chunks from the worker's base arena via `dva_arena_adopt`, and frees the worker's descriptor.
- **Explicit handle ownership & synchronization**: `Arena` and `Pool` descriptors contain unsynchronized mutable metadata (`offset`, `num_chunks`, `free_stack`, generation stacks). An explicit `Arena` or `Pool` must be owned by one thread at a time or protected with external synchronization if shared across threads.

## Fixed-capacity object pools

Pools manage uniform, fixed-size element allocations with $O(1)$ allocation and deallocation.

```{.dva .run}
#type Pool (buffer: Addr, free_stack: Addr, active: Addr, state: Addr,
   elem_size: Int, capacity: Int)
```

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mem::pool` | `Int, Int => Pool` | Creates pool: `mem::pool(elem_size, capacity)` |
| `mem::pool_alloc` | `Pool => < Addr | >` | Allocates slot: `<+ Addr +>` or `<-->` on full |
| `mem::pool_free` | `Pool, Addr => <>` | Frees slot: `<+>` on success, `<->` on error |
| `mem::pool_count` | `Pool => Int` | Number of currently active allocated slots |
| `mem::pool_capacity` | `Pool => Int` | Maximum capacity of the pool |
| `mem::pool_for_each` | `Pool, (Addr => ()) => ()` | Iterates over each active allocated slot |
| `mem::pool_destroy` | `Pool => ()` | Releases pool memory buffer |

```{.dva .run}
#use mem
#use io

// Create pool with element size 16 bytes and capacity of 4 slots:
p = mem::pool(16, 4)

io::out $ mem::pool_capacity(p) // 4
io::out $ mem::pool_count(p)    // 0

slot = mem::pool_alloc(p)
slot
   | addr =>
      @[addr] = 42
      io::out $ @[addr Int]
      freed = mem::pool_free(p, addr)
      freed | io::out("freed") | io::out("invalid")
   | io::out("pool exhausted")

mem::pool_destroy(p)
```
